yc-lyon.name: Lyon
yc-lyon.oneLiner: Foundation models on enterprise transaction data.
yc-lyon.thesis: Trains proprietary foundation models directly on a customer's own transaction/event data (28B transactions for one fintech, plus a major insurer pilot), beating rules-based baselines 4x on premium-card conversion. Small team but real enterprise traction is a strong early signal in a crowded vertical-AI space.

yc-herdr.name: herdr
yc-herdr.thesis: Open agent runtime with genuine bottom-up adoption (25k GitHub stars, 340k downloads, 500+ community plugins) and already closed a $6M seed led by Bessemer with a strong angel syndicate. Infra bet on agent fleets becoming standard dev workflow; main risk is monetizing an OSS-first project against well-funded competitors.

yc-useforward.name: Forward
yc-useforward.thesis: Agentic matching between borrowers and private-credit funds, built by founders with direct deal-diligence experience ($1B+) and a 5-person team already shipping. Real workflow pain point in an underdigitized market, but conservative buyers and long enterprise sales cycles are a risk.

hn-49833867.name: Whiteboard (YC W26) – An open-source IDE for thoughtful software design
hn-49833867.thesis: Open-source IDE (YC W26) that lets coding agents draw architecture/sequence diagrams of their own changes for review - a timely wedge as teams struggle to review AI-generated code. Strong Show HN reception (415 points) and built on VS Code/CodeOSS for fast distribution, though it competes for attention in a busy devtools category.

yc-agent-relay.name: Agent Relay
yc-agent-relay.oneLiner: The infrastructure to run coding agents for your team
yc-agent-relay.thesis: Messaging/infra layer for coordinating fleets of coding agents, already open-source with real GitHub adoption and a public enterprise partnership (Coder) covered by GlobeNewswire. Agent-orchestration infra is a hot, well-funded category and this team already has a distribution channel through Coder.

yc-rystic.name: Rystic
yc-rystic.oneLiner: API simulators for testing and training agents locally
yc-rystic.thesis: Local, stateful simulators of third-party APIs (Stripe, GitHub, Slack, Kalshi, etc.) for testing and training agents without hitting production services. Narrow but real pain point for every team building agents; named integrations suggest actual usage rather than a toy demo.

yc-talos-us.name: Talos
yc-talos-us.thesis: Predictive maintenance hardware/software for large power transformers, a capital-intensive but high-value market (grid operators pay dearly to avoid unplanned outages). Hardware/enterprise sales cycles are slower, which tempers near-term funding odds, but the problem is real and durable.

yc-veltha.name: Veltha
yc-veltha.oneLiner: AI native TPA starting with workers comp
yc-veltha.thesis: AI-native TPA for workers' comp claims, founded by two ex-Palantir engineers with deployment experience at large institutions. Regulated-insurance niche has real budget and the team pedigree suggests it can navigate the compliance-heavy sales cycle.

yc-hopper.name: Hopper
yc-hopper.thesis: Trains speech models on a customer's own production call data for fast, specialized voice inference. Multiple open senior full-stack/voice-infra roles across job boards suggest real funded hiring and early customer traction.

yc-tilion.name: Tilion
yc-tilion.oneLiner: Super fast, unblockable browser infra for agents
yc-tilion.thesis: Recompiled Chromium ('Fortress') for undetectable agent browsing, with a shipped PyPI package and MCP server already in beta use. Crowded space (Kernel, Browserbase, Browser Use) keeps odds modest, but agent browser infra is a real and growing need.

yc-tire-swing.name: Tire Swing
yc-tire-swing.thesis: AI eligibility/compliance automation for affordable-housing operators (LIHTC, Section 8 recertification), positioned as a drop-in replacement for compliance consultants. Niche but sticky government-adjacent recurring revenue with a cybersecurity-background CEO.

yc-ufoai.name: UFO.ai
yc-ufoai.thesis: Open-source agent platform reachable via Slack/iMessage/terminal, positioned as team-wide agent infrastructure. Two-person team in an already crowded 'agent OS' category makes this the most speculative of this week's picks.

yc-keres.name: Keres
yc-keres.oneLiner: Kill the drone, keep the jet. Reusable unmanned interceptors.
yc-keres.thesis: Reusable, jet-class drone/cruise-missile interceptor aimed at the fast-growing counter-UAS market, positioned as a cheaper alternative to million-dollar missiles (cf. Anduril Roadrunner, Army Coyote). Already shows ~$125K raised pre-YC and a 3-person team; defense-tech capital is flowing freely in 2026, giving it a credible shot at a priced seed round.

yc-grep-ai.name: Grep AI
yc-grep-ai.oneLiner: Self-improving agents that automate tedious operational work
yc-grep-ai.thesis: Builds 'self-improving' agents that convert repetitive ops work into code and save frontier-model reasoning for exceptions, with a named live customer (IG, a UK brokerage, using it for compliance-alert review). A 6-person team and a concrete enterprise logo at this stage is unusually strong traction for a YC F26 candidate, de-risking the next raise.

yc-orca-aerospace.name: Orca Aerospace
yc-orca-aerospace.oneLiner: AI spacecraft operators that lives onboard the vehicle
yc-orca-aerospace.thesis: Onboard AI 'operators' that let satellites make mission decisions autonomously instead of relying on ground control, sold to spacecraft manufacturers/operators. Good timing as satellite constellations scale and ground-ops costs become the bottleneck; 5-person team is relatively large for this stage, suggesting real buildout already underway.

yc-archangel-health.name: Archangel Health
yc-archangel-health.oneLiner: Infra to make AI safe enough to practice medicine
yc-archangel-health.thesis: Sources and de-identifies physician-graded clinical data to license to medical-AI developers, and helps health systems post-train models on their own data under HIPAA. Addresses the real scarcity of high-quality labeled clinical data for medical AI, but as a 2-person team it needs to land data-licensing customers quickly to prove the model.

yc-deploy.name: Deploy
yc-deploy.thesis: Robotics-as-a-service deployment layer that lets customers pay for robot labor as an opex line rather than buying hardware, hardware-agnostic across robot makers. Timely wedge (robotics deployment is genuinely underserved) but thin team of two and a capital-intensive services model make this the most speculative pick this week; sized as the smallest cheque.

yc-boat.name: Boat
yc-boat.oneLiner: The best cloud VMs for billions of agents
yc-boat.thesis: Cloud VMs purpose-built for AI coding agents (Claude Code, Codex, OpenCode) with disk-level forking and a CLI/SDK -- rides the same agent-sandbox wave as E2B/Daytona. Infra picks-and-shovels plays in this space have been raising quickly; team of 3, real product with published pricing.

yc-sona8.name: Sona8
yc-sona8.oneLiner: Voice agents survey employees to map, improve & automate workflows
yc-sona8.thesis: AI voice agents interview employees to map workflows for consulting/PE/transformation teams; already has a named pilot (several hundred interviews at a professional services firm) and MIT Sandbox backing. Team of 4 (founders + founding engineer) is more de-risked than typical solo YC teams.

yc-openseo.name: OpenSEO
yc-openseo.oneLiner: Open source alternative to Semrush and Ahrefs
yc-openseo.thesis: Open-source Semrush/Ahrefs alternative (MIT licensed, self-host or $10/mo) with an MCP server for agent-driven SEO workflows. Real GitHub traction claimed and a clean open-core monetization path, though data is a thin layer over DataForSEO so differentiation risk is real.

yc-sintropix.name: Sintropix
yc-sintropix.oneLiner: Autonomous accounting platform for global companies
yc-sintropix.thesis: AI-native ERP/autonomous accounting platform for LatAm SMBs with an AI assistant (Erwin) for financial Q&A; founders report 10 paying clients across Chile, Mexico, Brazil and the US, which is unusually concrete traction for this stage.

yc-quivly-ai.name: Quivly AI
yc-quivly-ai.oneLiner: AI agents that run onboarding, adoption, and renewals
yc-quivly-ai.thesis: Post-sales AI agents handling onboarding, usage-drop detection and renewal prep for usage-based B2B companies; launched Oct 8 2026 with working Slack/web/MCP integrations and a differentiated 'Radar' expansion-detection feature. Crowded post-sales-AI category is the main risk.

yc-blinka.name: Blinka
yc-blinka.oneLiner: Banking for US companies operating globally
yc-blinka.thesis: US-dollar banking infrastructure for Latin American companies with complex cross-border entity structures; founders report $10M+ processed in the first two months with a closed pilot group of 25 companies, which is unusually strong traction pre-Demo-Day. Fintech-for-LatAm-SMBs is a proven wedge (cf. Clara, Pomelo) and the brothers already have real-world banking/ops experience.

yc-pomerado.name: Pomerado
yc-pomerado.oneLiner: Turn any website into an MCP for your agents, in minutes
yc-pomerado.thesis: Open-source (MIT) tool that turns any website, including login/2FA-gated ones, into a deterministic MCP integration for AI agents; has a working GitHub repo, docs site, and a hosted Cloud tier. Rides the fast-growing agent-tooling/MCP ecosystem where distribution via open source is a credible wedge, though monetization of the open-core is still unproven.

yc-shepherd-robotics.name: Shepherd Robotics
yc-shepherd-robotics.oneLiner: Robots for high skilled labor powering AI infrastructure
yc-shepherd-robotics.thesis: General-purpose robots aimed at AI-infrastructure labor (data center build/ops, cable and wire harness assembly, kitting/packaging) with demonstrated wire-insertion and PCB-kitting capability. Timely 'robots to build the AI buildout' thesis that YC and other investors have been chasing hard this cycle; capital-intensive hardware raises risk but also means strong follow-on potential if milestones land.

yc-graypass.name: GrayPass
yc-graypass.oneLiner: Verify the expected person is still in control before sensitive…
yc-graypass.thesis: Continuous, passwordless identity verification (cognitive/behavioral biometrics) that reconfirms the expected human is still in control before a sensitive action completes. As AI agents increasingly take real-world actions on people's behalf, verifying a human (not a hijacked agent/session) is in the loop becomes a real security primitive; small team and unproven enterprise sales motion are the main risks.

yc-praxis.name: Praxis
yc-praxis.oneLiner: AI agents that run law firm operations.
yc-praxis.thesis: AI agents automating law-firm operations (intake, onboarding, billing) rather than legal research/drafting, which differentiates it from well-capitalized legal-research players like Harvey and Legora. Smallest cheque of the week given the crowded legal-AI field and a two-person team; a toe-hold bet on the ops-automation angle rather than the core legal-research battleground.

yc-telamont.name: Telamont
yc-telamont.oneLiner: Sentry for errors in construction documents
yc-telamont.thesis: AI that reads construction contracts, specs and drawings to flag conflicts and risks before disputes or rework, with integrations into Procore/Autodesk and visible construction-firm client logos already on the site. Team of 6 and a clear enterprise wedge (notice drafting, RFIs) in a space where a direct comparable (Primepoint) just closed a $10M seed, suggesting real investor appetite for this niche.

yc-organizely.name: Organizely
yc-organizely.oneLiner: A New AI-Native ERP for American Manufacturers 🇺🇸
yc-organizely.thesis: AI-native ERP for growing manufacturers (inventory, BOMs, planning, purchasing, maintenance) built by three co-founders who ran their own factory for six years -- strong founder-market fit. Already has a named customer (Kinetic Labs) citing margin and time savings, which is more traction than most pre-demo-day YC companies show this early.

yc-cesara.name: Cesara
yc-cesara.oneLiner: Faster & accurate transactions for health systems
yc-cesara.thesis: Governed agentic AI for hospital revenue-cycle and managed-care teams: checks claims/remits against payer contracts to catch underpayments and draft appeals. Enterprise-grade positioning (SOC2 Type II, HIPAA BAA, Epic/Oracle Health/MEDITECH integrations) and endorsements from former health-system CIOs suggest a team that can actually sell into hospitals, a notoriously hard market to crack.

yc-simantic.name: Simantic
yc-simantic.thesis: Runs real firmware on virtual microcontrollers for CI/CD and AI coding agents, plus an AI code reviewer that tests firmware PRs in the simulator. Rides the coding-agent infrastructure wave, but the embedded/firmware niche is smaller than the other picks, so sized as the smallest cheque.

state.lastRunNotes: Researched ~10 of this week's 36 YC Fall 2026 candidates via company sites and web search; skipped the Show HN/Product Hunt novelty projects and the storytold/*craft GitHub repos (suspiciously round star counts on repos created within the last 2 months, no independent company evidence, treated as likely fake-star farming rather than investable companies). Backed four B2B enterprise-SaaS picks with real founder-market fit and verifiable product depth: Telamont (construction contract/drawing risk AI, enterprise integrations, validated by a comparable company's $10M seed in the same niche), Organizely (AI ERP for manufacturers, founders ran a factory for 6 years, has a named customer case study), Cesara (healthcare revenue-cycle AI with notable health-system CIO endorsements, SOC2/HIPAA), and Simantic (embedded firmware simulation for AI coding agents, smaller niche so smaller cheque). Checked all 27 existing holdings for news; found no independently verifiable raises, shutdowns, or acquisitions for any of them (several aggregator sites like Dealroom/VCBacked/RoundFunded show unverified 'reconstructed' profiles, which don't meet the evidence-URL bar) -- consistent with YC Fall 2026 demo day not yet having happened. No follow-ons this week.
